circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street course situated around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, holding an FIA Grade 1 licence. It annually hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting motorsport series and races.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg, Austria, originally opened as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually from 1970 to 1987. Following a reconstruction and renaming to the A1-Ring, the venue returned to hosting the championship race from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is an urban street course situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, spanning 6. 003 km per lap and ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The track first hosted the 2016 European Grand Prix before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix. The track, which maintains a FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple configurations, has also accommodated various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and 24-hour endurance events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located near Barcelona in Spain, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing multiple racing disciplines. Holding an FIA Grade 1 license, the circuit can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian motorsport venue, stretching over 7 kilometres through the Walloon region, has been a Formula One staple since the sport's inception in 1950. The track currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix annually, with unbroken participation since 1985 aside from 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometres and serves as the home of the FIA Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships, open-wheel competitions, and stock car events throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit, located in Shanghai's Jiading district, is China's premier racing venue. It hosted the Chinese Grand Prix annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming from 2024, and has also begun accommodating the Shanghai ePrix electric racing championship since 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing venue situated in Northamptonshire that has been the traditional home of the British Grand Prix since 1948, notably hosting the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with other British circuits between 1955 and 1986, the Grand Prix established a permanent base at Silverstone from 1987 onwards. The track continues to host major motorsport events including MotoGP races.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Hungary, is a 4. 381 km circuit that hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, making it the fastest-constructed Formula One venue, the track was established outside the city along a major highway after initial plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park were rejected.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility. It has hosted the Italian Grand Prix nearly every year since 1949, making it one of Formula One's most enduring venues, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its characteristically long straights and fast-flowing corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which holds 155,000 spectators, hosts prominent Formula One and Super Formula racing competitions.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, following portions of the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its iconic hotels and casinos. The 3. 8-mile layout incorporates several of the destination's most recognizable venues, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, creating a uniquely themed racing environment amid the city's entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring racing brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix during three distinct eras, most recently from 2015 onwards on its current layout, with the event now known as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens featuring 3. 363 miles of track with 19 corners, designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One racing. The venue joined the championship calendar in 2022 and averages qualifying speeds around 139 mph, while also hosting a modified layout for electric racing series events beginning in 2025–26.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: Monaco's street circuit winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts along the harbor, covering 3. 337 kilometers of urban roads in the principality. The track is widely known as "Monte Carlo" despite technically being situated in Monaco, as much of the layout traverses the Monte Carlo neighborhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes northwest of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the resurrected Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026. The layout, featuring steeply banked corners and significant elevation changes as it traverses the North Sea dunes, earned it the nickname "Roller coaster in the Dunes" among Formula One enthusiasts.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated north of Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419 km FIA Grade 1 facility featuring a 1. 068 km main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed to commemorate deceased Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The counterclockwise circuit has hosted numerous grand prix events and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to another Brazilian racing legend, Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since its introduction in 2021. The circuit also began hosting an international electric racing championship event in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang planning zones into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design featuring extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the home venue for Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP, NASCAR, and endurance racing series, and has previously accommodated various other racing championships including IndyCar and sports car competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver competing in Formula One for the Williams team, racing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories across his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One World Drivers' Championship with Mercedes in 2026, setting a record as the sport's youngest champion. Since entering the series in 2025, he has claimed nine Grand Prix victories for the team.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto competes in Formula One, currently racing for the Audi team in the championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes for Cadillac in Formula One and has achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his 2019 and 2020 campaigns with Mercedes. Across his 13-season career, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan competes in endurance racing for AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series LMP2 category, having previously raced in the European Le Mans Series. He holds the position of reserve driver at Haas and made seven Formula One starts during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The French competitor achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian racing driver who represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton, a British driver, represents Ferrari in Formula One competition and holds an unprecedented seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He leads the sport across multiple statistical categories, including victories, front-row starts, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One, bringing considerable experience from his successful endurance racing career, which included a Le Mans 24 Hours victory with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born driver currently racing in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship. Across his nine seasons in the sport, Leclerc has secured nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: K-Mag is a Danish driver competing in endurance racing for BMW through WRT and occasionally in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing. He previously spent two separate stints in Formula One, racing from 2014 to 2020 before returning for the 2022 and 2023 seasons.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently competing for McLaren, claimed the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2025. Throughout his eight-season career, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon has competed in Formula One for Haas in recent years, following a successful stint with Alpine where he claimed victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac after a lengthy career spanning 15 seasons. He finished second in the 2023 World Drivers' Championship while driving for Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver competing for McLaren who has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One over fourteen years between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his tenure in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has competed in Formula One for Mercedes, securing victories in eight separate championship seasons throughout his career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. Throughout his 12-season career, he has secured four Grand Prix victories.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous stints in IMSA's LMP2 class. He competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to sports car racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who currently holds a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After completing a full-time racing stint in the championship from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a reserve role starting in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian racing driver Max Verstappen competes for Red Bull Racing, where he has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles spanning 2021 through 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently serving as a reserve driver for Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone, this French-backed team has competed under the Alpine banner since 2021 after being renamed from its previous Renault identity to highlight the luxury sports car marque. The squad functioned as Renault's official works entry throughout this period until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has made multiple attempts at Formula One competition throughout the sport's history, with the current incarnation operating as a British-registered team competing under the Aramco partnership banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing operations of Italian manufacturer Ferrari in Formula One, famously recognized by their "Prancing Horse" emblem. As the sport's longest-running and most accomplished team, Ferrari has participated continuously in every World Championship season since the series began in 1950.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American Formula One team in 2014, making its competitive debut in 2016. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal, leading the squad into a new era of competition.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss motorsport engineering firm established in 1970, this independent constructor achieved notable success in endurance racing, including a 1989 Le Mans victory with Mercedes-Benz, before joining Formula One in 1993. The team competed in the sport for over three decades, becoming one of the oldest constructors by race count, until ceasing operations in 2025 when Audi acquired its operations to establish their own competitive program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under sponsorship arrangements. The team operates as part of the wider McLaren Group, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 through both factory teams and engine supply arrangements. The current team, competing as Mercedes-AMG Petronas from its Brackley base under a German licence, restructured its ownership in 2022 to include equal stakes held by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff. The marque's racing teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024 as part of Red Bull's multi-team strategy, operating alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the squad functions as Red Bull GmbH's second racing entity in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates as an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and is part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio alongside Racing Bulls. Founded in 2005, the team was led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies subsequently assuming the role of team principal.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based at Grove in Oxfordshire, the team competes in the 2026 season as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and remains one of the grid's established operations.
